entry.what: The maintainer handed the build-out to a coordinating session: one subagent per step of docs/plan.xml, in order, committing and pushing to main, until a Python host and a Node host talk to each other through their transports.
entry.why: The maintainer cannot supervise; issues and uncertainties are logged here for later review.

entry.what: tools/planxml.py edits docs/plan.xml (Plan) and docs/log.xml (Log), each validated against its schema before it is written.

Expose ta_address_format and ta_address_format_name as Address.fromSession(system, session) and Address.fromName(system, name), static constructors of the Address type (decision d-address); p0-map writes their planned row.
entry.why: An application with a transport addresses an actor on another system by its system id and session or name. d-address made the Address core's parser behind a JavaScript type so that no application parses the grammar; formatting it by hand (percent-encoding a name, the #_scxml_ prefix) is the same grammar written the other way, and core has the function. Not instance properties: .session and .name are the parts already. Python has no counterpart (its Address takes text only), so the two bindings differ until Python adds it or the maintainer refuses it here.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/address.h (ta_address_format, ta_address_format_name, ta_buffer out); tinyactors-cpython/src/value_types.c:41-60 (Address(text) only); docs/plan.xml decision d-address.

entry.what: quickjs: ta_datamodel_ecmascript_heap_bytes behind an API item (a read of the engine's heap on a datamodel "quickjs" host, named in p0-map); ta_datamodel_ecmascript_last_error used internally, as the message of the TinyactorsError that hibernate(), snapshot() or a migration failure gives with TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED on quickjs; ta_datamodel_ecmascript_set_memory_limit not exposed.
entry.why: quickjs is the sandbox (d-datamodel), whose limits are passed at creation (ta_datamodel_ecmascript_config: max_ops, memory_limit, realm); an operator watching a sandboxed host against its limit needs the usage, which is O(1). last_error says which variable could not be stored: it improves an error the API already raises, with no new item. Changing the limit on a running host has no need shown (the creation option covers the sandbox), so it stays out until one is. Python exposes none of the three and raises a bare TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/datamodel_ecmascript.h:118-128; docs/plan.xml decision d-datamodel ("quickjs as a sandbox needs its limits passed through"); tinyactors-cpython/src/host.c:508-511 (a zeroed config).

entry.what: Expose ta_http_encode_post and ta_http_parse_request as two functions of the module (the POST of a BasicHTTP send, and the event of an incoming request), for an application's HTTP I/O processor and the adapter's W3C BasicHTTP loopback; p0-map names them.
entry.why: BasicHTTP is SCXML's standard I/O processor (C.2), the codec is in core, transport-agnostic and freestanding, and the root rule says code free of any language's API belongs in a C layer, not in a binding. Without it an application (and the adapter) writes the form encoding again in JavaScript. This departs from Python's precedent: Python's adapter encodes and parses BasicHTTP in Python.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/basic_http.h; tinyactors-cpython/conform/__main__.py:404-429 (BasicHTTP written in Python); root AGENTS.md, "Layers".

entry.what: ta_host_segment_count and ta_host_snapshot_segments are not exposed, as Python decided.
entry.why: host.stats has segments; Host.restore reads the images from the pack itself (ta_host_snapshot_image), so nothing needs the hashes.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/ROADMAP.md, "The API review (2026-10-15)", last paragraph.

entry.what: ta_xml_writer_* are not exposed now: the chart builder that would use them is the convenience layer's, after M1 and when the maintainer picks it, and the direct layer gains an item over the writer in that change.
entry.why: An application writes chart text today; no need for the writer is shown before the builder exists, and the direct layer mirrors core only where an item uses it (d-layers).
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/compile.h:84-110; docs/plan.xml decision d-layers; tinyactors-cpython/AGENTS.md, "Layers" (the same deferral).

entry.what: Two internal uses the plan did not name: ta_runtime_now_ns is the wall clock of a host given no clock (src/loop.c, as Python's loop.c), and ta_host_snapshot with an empty buffer is snapshot()'s quiescence check before any datamodel state is built (as Python's host.c).
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/src/loop.c:119; tinyactors-cpython/src/host.c:1342.

entry.what: The same scan applies to the Python binding: its docs/api-map.md lists only ta_host_resume, ta_host_locate, ta_host_system, ta_actor_info_get and ta_host_segment_info_get as used internally, and names no not-exposed functions except in ROADMAP.md. Its src calls 97 of core's 230 public functions; the three lists of tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md ("Every public function of core") can be carried over with Python's file names, and the decisions above (Address from parts, quickjs's heap and last error, BasicHTTP) asked of Python too. tinyactors-cpython was not edited.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/docs/api-map.md (the list under the table); a scan of tinyactors-cpython/src for calls of the names in tinyactors-core/include/*.api.json.

entry.what: The quickjs sandbox's limits are the Host option quickjs: {maxOps, memoryLimit, stackLimit, realm: 'auto' | 'isolated'}, each field ta_datamodel_ecmascript_config's (max_ops, memory_limit, stack_limit, realm), an absent field core's default 0; given with datamodel 'native' it throws TypeError at creation.
entry.why: d-datamodel says the limits are passed through from the Host's option but names no shape. One nested object keeps the sandbox's settings together and mirrors the C struct field by field (camelCase); abort_flag is not exposed (no JavaScript caller can set a C flag asynchronously). A TypeError for a quickjs option on a native host refuses a setting that would otherwise be silently ignored.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/datamodel_ecmascript.h:61-72; docs/plan.xml decision d-datamodel; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: ta_datamodel_ecmascript_heap_bytes is the getter host.quickjsHeapBytes (a number, read on each access), undefined on a native host.
entry.why: l-p0-inventory-quickjs-limits decided to expose the read and left the name to p0-map. A getter, not a method, because the read is O(1) and has no effect; the quickjs prefix says it is the sandbox's, not the host's memory.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/datamodel_ecmascript.h:124; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: BasicHTTP is encodeHTTPPost({url, event, fields, body}) returning the request's bytes (a Buffer copied once from the call's arena), and parseHTTPRequest(message) returning {method, target, body, event, fields}; fields are arrays of {name, value} strings, as ta_http_field; a refusal throws TinyactorsError with TA_ERROR_INVALID.
entry.why: l-p0-inventory-basic-http decided to expose the codec and left the names to p0-map. The names follow the root acronym rule (HTTP in capitals); an array of {name, value} keeps order and repeated names, which a plain object would lose.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/basic_http.h; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: host.sendMany(items) takes an array of objects of host.send(message)'s fields ({target, event, data, sendid, origin, traceparent}), not Python's tuples.
entry.why: JavaScript has no tuples; one shape for send(message), sendMany's items and send.message means a transport can batch what it received unchanged.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/docs/api-map.md, row Host.send_many; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: send.answer, invocation.sendBack and invocation.done keep the send's (or invocation's) trace unless the options give traceparent; traceparent: null starts a new trace; an absent or undefined traceparent keeps it.
entry.why: AGENTS.md says an answer keeps the trace 'unless the caller passes none' without saying how none is written. In JavaScript undefined means absent (an options object spread with a missing key), so null is the explicit 'none', as Python's traceparent=None is.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md, 'Layers and the resolver', the traceparent bullet; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: host.ticksPerSecond and host.closed are in the API, as Python's Host.ticks_per_second and Host.closed are; the plan's api section did not list them.
entry.why: Python's adapter converts the driver's monotonic ticks with ticks_per_second, and closed is how an application knows a close deferred from a handler happened. Borrowed from Python, not invented: host.config behind one, ta_host_free behind the other.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/docs/api-map.md, row Host.ticks_per_second, Host.closed; tinyactors-cpython/conform/__main__.py:182; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: An exhausted pool (TA_RUN_EXHAUSTED) is reported as TinyactorsError with status TA_ERROR_NO_MEMORY and the pool's name in the message, where Python raises MemoryError naming the pool.
entry.why: JavaScript has no MemoryError; RangeError is what engines throw for an allocation they refuse, but it carries no status to branch on. A TinyactorsError keeps one error type for core's reports, and the host stays usable as in Python.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/AGENTS.md, 'The loop' table (TA_PYTHON_NEXT_EXHAUSTED); tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/system.h (TA_RUN_EXHAUSTED, TA_POOL_*); tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: new Address(text) takes any text (parts undefined when it is no address); Address.fromSession(system, session: bigint) and Address.fromName(system, name) throw TinyactorsError with TA_ERROR_INVALID when core's formatter refuses; an Address is not a Value, so encode and a payload refuse it.
entry.why: d-address follows Python's Address(text); tag 32 is never written by Node (values.txt, ECMAScript), so an Address inside data has no encoding and is refused rather than turned into a string silently.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/address.h:45-60; docs/plan.xml decision d-address; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: host.send's options are {sendid, traceparent, origin} (Python's keywords, sendid included, which the plan's item omitted), and host.fail(target, sendid?) takes the sendid as optional, as Python's sendid=None.
entry.why: sendid is ta_event_in's field and send.message carries it, so send(target, ...) and send(message) take the same fields.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/docs/api-map.md, rows Host.send and Host.fail; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: index.d.ts declares Compiled, Send, LogEntry, Migrated, Invocation, Service, ChartRef and MigrationResult as interfaces (no constructor exported); TinyactorsError, CompileError, ResolveError, Address, SimulatedClock and Host as classes. TinyactorsError's constructor is (message, {code, reason, path, status}); ResolveError's (message, {line, column}); ChartRef is {segment, chart}.
entry.why: Only what an application constructs or tests with instanceof is a class; the rest the addon makes. Options objects in place of Python's keyword arguments, as the plan's ResolveError item already writes.
entry.evidence: docs/plan.xml section api, items a-resolver, a-error; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: host.snapshot() labels its datamodel state tinyactors-napi, as Python's is labelled tinyactors-cpython, and Host.restore refuses a pack another program labelled.
entry.why: A native datamodel's state is the addon's own CBOR, which another binding cannot read.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/AGENTS.md, 'Snapshots'; tinyactors-napi/docs/api-map.md (its row); tinyactors-napi/index.d.ts

entry.what: GATE in mise/napi.rb holds no suite (suites: []), so mise run test skips the conformance run; it was protocol and scenarios before any adapter existed.
entry.why: With conform.mjs present the test task runs the gate, and an adapter that answers -32601 to everything passes no case: the runner fails a suite that passes nothing ('proves nothing') and a binding that does not offer host.create. The brief allowed emptying it; the next step (p1-host) raises it again as host.create and the protocol vectors' methods land.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-test/lib/runner.rb:347-359 (summary, REQUIRED); mise run conform -- --milestone M1 --suite protocol: 'protocol: 0 pass, 0 fail, 140 skip ... FAIL no case passed in protocol ... FAIL not offered, but a binding must offer: host.create'

entry.what: encode has no host, so its writer and its strings live in a ta_growable_arena of the environment's instance (module.c), a mark per call, released on every path; the allocator (malloc and free with napi_adjust_external_memory) lives in module.c too, with the instance as its context, for every host to share. The allocation lint names module.c's ta_napi_allocator_alloc/_free and ta_napi_instance_new/_finalize, and host.c's ta_napi_host_new/_finalize, instead of the removed handles.c and host.c's own allocator.
entry.why: The plan says 'in the call's arena' and the rulebook has one arena per host; a module-level call needs one arena outside any host. Python's encode uses a 256-byte stack room growing through the raw allocator instead; the arena keeps its chunks, so a warmed encode allocates nothing, and nested calls (a getter that encodes) nest marks.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/module.c, src/values.c (ta_napi_encode); tinyactors-cpython/src/values.c:132-147; test/values.test.mjs 'marks nest'

entry.what: TinyactorsError is defined once per environment by a constant script (napi_run_script of a class extending Error), referenced from the instance and exported; C throws it with napi_new_instance(message, {status: ta_status_name(...)}).
entry.why: A class made with napi_define_class is no Error (no stack, no [[ErrorData]]); class ... extends Error is the language's own way. The script is the addon's constant, not chart code; it runs on node 22.23.3 and bun 1.4.1.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/module.c (ta_napi_error_source); test/values.test.mjs 'TinyactorsError: an Error with ...' under both runtimes

entry.what: encode follows the rulebook's value table, not values.txt's encode cases, which are an ECMAScript datamodel's to_wire: it keeps undefined (f7, at the top, in arrays and as a key's value) and refuses a Date, a function, an ArrayBuffer, a DataView and typed arrays other than Uint8Array with TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED (to_wire writes null, drops, writes JSON or bytes). test/values.test.mjs lists those nine cases (DIFFERS) with what encode gives, and checks each name is still in values.txt. Refusals: TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED for a value outside the table, TA_ERROR_INVALID for one it cannot hold and for malformed CBOR (the reader's status passes through: an indefinite length is TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED); decode of a non-bytes argument is a TypeError; decode gives a plain Uint8Array, not a Buffer.
entry.why: AGENTS.md 'Values' and plan item a-values: undefined and null stay distinct, plain objects and arrays only, what cannot be written is refused, never turned into a value. For the next steps: the native datamodel's to_wire (p1-datamodel) needs values.txt's to_wire rules, a second mode of values.c; and the adapter's host.run sends must carry the sender's wire form, since encode(send.data) of a native payload holding undefined writes f7 where the echo expects f6 ('ECMAScript: undefined at the top is null').
entry.evidence: tinyactors-test/suites/protocol/values.txt (encode cases; header: 'encode and invalid cases are value.encode's ... on ECMAScript datamodels'); tinyactors-test/docs/driver.md:65 (value.encode is to_wire); tinyactors-napi/docs/values.md, 'encode and a datamodel's to_wire'

entry.what: A host whose datamodel is "native" (the default, so also new Host(config) with no datamodel option) throws TinyactorsError TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED until p1-datamodel builds the native datamodel; quickjs is never registered under the native name. Tests and the next steps pass datamodel: "quickjs".
entry.why: The brief offered either; registering quickjs as "native" would make tests pass for the wrong datamodel and hide which one ran. p1-datamodel removes the refusal and the test "the native datamodel is refused until it is built" in test/host.test.mjs.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/host.c (ta_napi_host_datamodel); test/host.test.mjs

entry.what: The allocator's context is the napi_env itself (ta_napi_allocator(env) in module.c), not the instance; the host struct is made and freed through it, so it is reported too.
entry.why: A host finalizer may run at the environment's teardown after or before the instance data's finalizer (order unverified across Node and Bun); with the env as context the finalizer never reads the instance.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/module.c (ta_napi_allocator); src/host.c (ta_napi_host_new, ta_napi_host_finalize)

entry.what: The handlers are one object on the wrapper under a Symbol("tinyactors.handlers") the instance keeps (in an object it references), non-enumerable, non-configurable, writable so close() sets it to undefined. It holds the handlers by name and processors, an array: processors[0] the transport, processors[i + 1] the handler of the config's ioProcessors[i] (core's IO_PROCESSOR numbering). The C side reaches the wrapper through a weak napi_ref (count 0).
entry.why: Node-API has no private symbols (an unexported Symbol is the nearest; Object.getOwnPropertySymbols still sees it); a napi_ref to a symbol needs Node-API 10, so the instance references an object holding it.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/host.c (ta_napi_host_keep, ta_napi_host_read_config); test/host.test.mjs "the handlers are the wrapper's"

entry.what: new Host refuses an option name it does not know (TypeError "unknown Host option: x"), and the quickjs option's too; a handler that is not a function, ioProcessors or services not objects of functions, and an ioProcessors type the config lacks are TypeErrors (Python: ValueError for the last). A non-native datamodel name other than "quickjs" is a TypeError.
entry.why: Python's keyword arguments refuse a misspelled name by themselves; an options bag ignores one silently, so a typo (ioprocessors) would drop a handler without a word.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/host.c (ta_napi_only_known); tinyactors-cpython/tests/test_host.py:181

entry.what: Node 22 does not show napi_adjust_external_memory's blocks in process.memoryUsage().external nor v8.getHeapStatistics().external_memory (50 hosts: +40 bytes), Bun does (+347 KB, back to +3 KB after collection). The test checks collection with a FinalizationRegistry on both and the memory where the runtime shows it. A spike that printed napi_adjust_external_memory's adjusted total on node showed 10992 bytes before 5 hosts, 221568 with them, and 10648 after gc: the finalizer frees every block.
entry.why: The done-when asks that a dropped host frees its memory under both runtimes; on node it is shown only by the counter Node-API returns.
entry.evidence: spike (scratchpad p1-host, a fprintf in ta_napi_allocator_alloc/_free, not committed): "adj 10992 ... adj 221568 created ... free 10648 collected"; test/host.test.mjs, the last case

entry.what: GATE stays empty: the adapter still offers no method. host.create alone cannot pass a suite, since the runner fails a binding kind that does not offer every method but value.encode (host.post, image.add, host.run, actor.spawn, scenario.run, w3c.run ...), so the gate is raised in p1-conform, when the adapter offers them all.
entry.why: The previous step expected p1-host to raise it.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-test/lib/runner.rb:37-40 (METHODS, REQUIRED), :357-359; tinyactors-napi/mise/napi.rb (GATE comment)

entry.what: close() frees the host, its tables (each row's napi_ref deleted first), quickjs and the arena, and drops the handlers; from inside a call (ta_napi_enter/_leave depth) or a turn it is deferred to the outermost leave. Not yet: trace.end and the last take of telemetry (with the encoder's step), clearing the timer and the deferral at the end of a turn (p1-loop sets host->turning), and the asyncDispose wait for the last take's promises: asyncDispose resolves at once. ta_napi_enter and ta_napi_leave exist for the next steps' calls; no method of p1-host enters (close and the getters touch no arena).
entry.why: The loop and the encoder are later steps; the api-map row says the last take is planned.
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/host.c (ta_napi_host_close, ta_napi_host_close_now, ta_napi_leave); docs/api-map.md row host.close()

entry.what: ta_napi_value_write takes a ta_napi_writing {writer, arena}: the arena of the call's text is the caller's (the module's arena for encode, the host's for a host's call), as the rulebook has one arena per host.
entry.why: values.c wrote text into the instance's arena whatever the caller; the API changed in place (root AGENTS.md).
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/addon.h (ta_napi_writing); src/values.c; src/host.c (ta_napi_host_create)

entry.what: The tables are made with rows the rulebook names, each a placeholder its step fills: chart {functions}, session {scope, chart}, payload {value, count}, loop {items}, pending {slot: the handlers' place on the wrapper}. Every row but pending holds its napi_ref first, which the host deletes at free.
entry.why: The brief asks for the tables now; their contents are p1-datamodel's and p1-methods', which may change the rows (the release in ta_napi_host_release assumes the reference first).
entry.evidence: tinyactors-napi/src/addon.h (ta_napi_*_row); src/host.c (ta_napi_rows_release)
